questions.stem: Osmosis is best defined as the movement of

options.text: solute particles from a dilute to a concentrated solution
water molecules from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
any substance against a concentration gradient using energy
gas particles from a region of low pressure to one of high pressure

questions.explanation: Osmosis is specifically about water and specifically requires a partially permeable membrane; the water moves towards the more concentrated solution because that side has the lower water potential. Any definition that omits either water or the membrane is incomplete.

distractorRationale.a: The solute cannot cross a partially permeable membrane; it is the water that moves
distractorRationale.c: This describes active transport, which requires energy from respiration
distractorRationale.d: Gases diffuse from high to low pressure, and this is not osmosis

questions.stem: A plant cell placed in distilled water becomes firm and swollen. This condition is described as
questions.explanation: Water enters by osmosis, the vacuole swells and presses the cytoplasm against the cellulose wall, and the wall pushes back. The resulting internal pressure makes the cell turgid, and it is this turgor that keeps soft-stemmed plants upright.

distractorRationale.a: Plasmolysis is the opposite: the cell has lost water in a concentrated solution
distractorRationale.c: A flaccid cell has lost water and is limp
distractorRationale.d: Haemolysis is the bursting of a red blood cell, which has no cell wall

questions.stem: The uptake of mineral ions by root hair cells stopped completely when the roots were treated with a respiratory poison. This shows that the ions were absorbed by
questions.explanation: Only active transport depends on ATP from respiration, so blocking respiration stops it. Soil solution is usually more dilute in ions than the root cell sap, so the ions have to be pumped in against the concentration gradient.

distractorRationale.a: Diffusion is passive and would carry on even with respiration blocked
distractorRationale.b: Osmosis involves water rather than mineral ions and is also passive
distractorRationale.d: Transpiration pull moves water up the xylem; it does not take ions into the cell

questions.stem: Visking tubing containing 20% sugar solution is placed in a beaker of 5% sugar solution. After 30 minutes the tubing will have

options.text: lost mass, because sugar moved out of the tubing
gained mass, because water moved into the tubing
gained mass, because sugar moved into the tubing
kept the same mass, because the membrane blocks all movement

questions.explanation: The 5% solution outside is the more dilute one, so it has the higher water potential and water crosses the partially permeable tubing into the 20% solution. Sugar molecules are too large to cross, so the tubing gains water and therefore gains mass.

distractorRationale.a: Sucrose molecules cannot pass through Visking tubing, so no sugar leaves
distractorRationale.c: Sugar moving in would require it to cross the membrane and to move up its gradient
distractorRationale.d: The membrane is partially permeable, not impermeable — water passes freely

questions.stem: Red blood cells placed in distilled water burst, but onion cells placed in distilled water do not. The reason is that onion cells

options.text: do not take in water by osmosis
have a rigid cellulose wall that resists the increase in pressure
contain chloroplasts that absorb the excess water

questions.explanation: Both cell types take in water by osmosis, but the plant cell is enclosed by an inelastic cellulose wall that pushes back once the cell is full, so pressure builds and inflow stops before bursting. A red blood cell has only a flexible membrane, so it keeps swelling until it ruptures.

distractorRationale.a: Onion cells do absorb water by osmosis — that is why they become turgid
distractorRationale.c: All living cells, including plant cells, have a cell membrane
distractorRationale.d: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis and do not absorb excess water

questions.stem: Which process is responsible for oxygen passing from the air in an alveolus into the blood in a nearby capillary?
questions.explanation: Air in the alveolus has a higher oxygen concentration than the blood arriving from the body, so oxygen diffuses down the gradient across the thin, moist alveolar wall. No energy is spent by the cell; the gradient is maintained by breathing and by blood flow.

distractorRationale.a: Movement is with the gradient, so no energy input is needed
distractorRationale.b: Osmosis refers to water movement, not oxygen
distractorRationale.d: Plasmolysis is the shrinking of a plant cell and is unrelated to gas exchange

questions.stem: A wilting hibiscus plant is watered and becomes upright again within an hour. Which sequence explains the recovery?

options.text: Water enters the cells by osmosis, the vacuoles swell, the cells become turgid and the stem is supported
Water enters by active transport, the cell walls thicken and the stem stiffens
Salts diffuse out of the cells, the sap becomes dilute and the cells become flaccid
The cells plasmolyse, which pushes the cytoplasm outwards against the wall

questions.explanation: Wilting means the cells have lost water and lost turgor. Adding water makes the soil solution more dilute than the cell sap, so water re-enters by osmosis, the vacuoles refill, turgor pressure is restored and the soft tissues once again support the stem.

distractorRationale.b: Water movement is passive, and cell walls do not thicken over an hour
distractorRationale.c: Losing salts and becoming flaccid would make the wilting worse, not better
distractorRationale.d: Plasmolysis is the loss of water that caused the wilting in the first place

questions.stem: Fresh cucumber slices sprinkled with salt release water because water moves out of the cucumber cells by osmosis.
questions.explanation: True. The salt dissolves in the film of moisture on the surface to give a very concentrated solution, which has a lower water potential than the cell sap. Water therefore leaves the cells by osmosis, they lose turgor, and the slices become limp.

questions.stem: Fluid given to a patient through a drip must be isotonic with blood plasma. What would happen if pure distilled water were used instead?

options.text: The red blood cells would shrink and become crenated
The red blood cells would take in water by osmosis and burst
Nothing, because red blood cells have cell walls
The plasma would become more concentrated

questions.explanation: Distilled water has a much higher water potential than the cytoplasm of a red blood cell, so water floods in by osmosis. With no cell wall to resist the pressure the membrane ruptures — haemolysis — releasing haemoglobin into the plasma.

distractorRationale.a: Crenation happens in a solution that is more concentrated than the cell, not in distilled water
distractorRationale.c: Red blood cells are animal cells and have no cell wall
distractorRationale.d: Adding water dilutes the plasma rather than concentrating it

questions.stem: Which pair of statements correctly distinguishes diffusion from active transport?

options.text: Both need energy, but only diffusion needs a membrane
Diffusion needs no energy and follows the gradient; active transport needs energy and works against the gradient
Diffusion needs energy and works against the gradient; active transport needs none
Both work against the concentration gradient, but only active transport involves water

questions.explanation: The two distinguishing features are the energy requirement and the direction relative to the gradient, and they always go together: moving a substance uphill against its gradient is the reason energy is needed. Diffusion simply exploits gradients that already exist.

distractorRationale.a: Diffusion requires no energy, and it can occur with or without a membrane
distractorRationale.c: The two processes have been swapped
distractorRationale.d: Diffusion follows the gradient, and active transport moves ions and solutes rather than water

questions.stem: What is the primary difference between diffusion and osmosis?

options.text: Diffusion involves the movement of solutes, while osmosis involves the movement of water.
Diffusion requires energy, while osmosis does not.
Osmosis can occur in gases, while diffusion cannot.
Diffusion only occurs in liquids, while osmosis occurs in solids.

questions.explanation: Diffusion is the movement of solute particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration, while osmosis specifically refers to the movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane. Understanding this distinction is crucial in studying how substances move in biological systems.

distractorRationale.b: Osmosis is a passive process and does not require energy, whereas diffusion also does not require energy.
distractorRationale.c: Osmosis is limited to the movement of water, which typically occurs in liquid solutions.
distractorRationale.d: Both diffusion and osmosis can occur in liquids, but osmosis specifically involves water.

questions.stem: In which direction will water move if a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution?

options.text: Water movement will depend on temperature.

questions.explanation: When a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, water moves out of the cell to the area of higher solute concentration, leading to plasmolysis. This movement is essential for understanding how cells maintain their turgor pressure and overall health.

distractorRationale.a: Water does not move into the cell in a hypertonic solution; it moves out.
distractorRationale.c: There will be movement of water out of the cell due to the concentration gradient.
distractorRationale.d: Temperature does not affect the direction of water movement in this context.

questions.stem: What happens to a red blood cell when placed in a hypotonic solution?
questions.explanation: In a hypotonic solution, the concentration of solutes outside the red blood cell is lower than inside, causing water to move into the cell. This influx of water can lead to swelling and potentially bursting, known as hemolysis.

distractorRationale.a: A red blood cell does not shrink in a hypotonic solution; it swells.
distractorRationale.b: The cell cannot remain the same as water will move into it.
distractorRationale.d: Turgidity is a term used for plant cells, not red blood cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about active transport is true?

options.text: It requires energy to move substances against their concentration gradient.
It occurs only in plant cells.
It does not involve any proteins.

questions.explanation: Active transport is the process by which cells move substances against their concentration gradient, which requires energy, typically from ATP. This mechanism is crucial for maintaining cellular functions and homeostasis.

distractorRationale.b: Active transport occurs in both plant and animal cells.
distractorRationale.c: Active transport is not passive; it requires energy.
distractorRationale.d: Active transport often involves specific transport proteins.

questions.stem: What is plasmolysis in plant cells?

options.text: The process of water entering the cell.
The shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall.

questions.explanation: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell loses water in a hypertonic solution, causing the cytoplasm to shrink and pull away from the cell wall. This process is significant as it leads to wilting and loss of turgor pressure in plants.

distractorRationale.a: Plasmolysis is specifically about water leaving the cell, not entering.
distractorRationale.c: Bursting of the cell is called lysis, not plasmolysis.
distractorRationale.d: Photosynthesis is unrelated to the concept of plasmolysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes turgidity in plant cells?

options.text: The cell is limp and wilted.
The cell is swollen and firm due to water uptake.
The cell is bursting due to excess water.
The cell has shrunk due to water loss.

questions.explanation: Turgidity refers to the state of a plant cell when it is filled with water, making it firm and providing structural support. This condition is essential for maintaining the plant's upright posture and overall health.

distractorRationale.a: A limp and wilted cell indicates a lack of turgor pressure.
distractorRationale.c: Bursting is not a stable state and indicates cell damage.
distractorRationale.d: Shrinking indicates plasmolysis, not turgidity.

questions.stem: Which of the following processes requires a membrane protein?
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion requires specific membrane proteins to help transport molecules across the cell membrane, especially for larger or polar molecules that cannot easily pass through the lipid bilayer. This process is crucial for the uptake of essential nutrients by cells.

distractorRationale.a: Simple diffusion does not require any proteins; it occurs freely across membranes.
distractorRationale.c: Osmosis can occur through the membrane without the need for proteins.
distractorRationale.d: Passive diffusion is a general term that includes processes that do not require proteins.

questions.stem: What term describes the movement of molecules from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration?
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the process by which molecules move from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration until equilibrium is reached. This process is fundamental to many biological functions, including gas exchange and nutrient absorption.

distractorRationale.a: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient, requiring energy.
distractorRationale.c: Endocytosis involves the engulfing of substances by the cell membrane.
distractorRationale.d: Exocytosis is the process of expelling substances from the cell.

questions.stem: What occurs during the process of active transport?

options.text: Substances move down their concentration gradient.
Energy is used to move substances against their concentration gradient.
Substances move freely across the membrane.

questions.explanation: Active transport requires energy to move substances against their concentration gradient, allowing cells to uptake necessary ions and nutrients even when they are in lower concentrations outside the cell. This process is vital for maintaining cellular functions.

distractorRationale.a: Moving down the concentration gradient is characteristic of passive transport, not active.
distractorRationale.c: Active transport specifically requires energy.
distractorRationale.d: Active transport involves selective movement, not free passage.

questions.stem: What is the result of placing a plant cell in a concentrated salt solution?
questions.explanation: When a plant cell is placed in a concentrated salt solution, water moves out of the cell, leading to plasmolysis where the cell membrane pulls away from the cell wall. This process is detrimental to plant health and can lead to wilting.

distractorRationale.a: Turgidity occurs when cells gain water, not lose it.
distractorRationale.c: The cell will change as water exits the cell.
distractorRationale.d: Bursting is not typical in plant cells; they undergo plasmolysis instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains the process of diffusion?

options.text: Movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane
Movement of molecules from an area of low concentration to high concentration
Movement of molecules from an area of high concentration to low concentration
Movement of solutes against the concentration gradient

questions.explanation: Diffusion is the passive movement of molecules from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration until equilibrium is reached. This process does not require energy and is fundamental to many biological functions.

distractorRationale.a: This describes osmosis, not diffusion.
distractorRationale.b: This is the opposite of how diffusion works.
distractorRationale.d: This describes active transport, which requires energy.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of osmosis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is crucial for maintaining turgor pressure in plant cells, which helps keep the plant upright and supports its structure. Turgor pressure is generated when water enters the cell, causing it to swell.

distractorRationale.a: Nutrient transport is primarily achieved through active transport.
distractorRationale.c: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts and is not directly related to osmosis.
distractorRationale.d: Respiration is a separate process that does not rely on osmosis.

questions.stem: In which situation would a plant cell undergo plasmolysis?

options.text: When placed in a hypertonic solution
When placed in an isotonic solution
When placed in a hypotonic solution

questions.explanation: Plasmolysis occurs when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, causing water to exit the cell. This results in the cell membrane pulling away from the cell wall, leading to wilting.

distractorRationale.a: In distilled water, the cell would become turgid, not plasmolyzed.
distractorRationale.c: In an isotonic solution, there would be no net movement of water.
distractorRationale.d: In a hypotonic solution, the cell would swell and become turgid.

Passive transport requires energy, while active transport does not

questions.explanation: Active transport requires energy (usually from ATP) to move substances against their concentration gradient, whereas passive transport occurs without energy input, allowing substances to move from high to low concentration.

distractorRationale.c: Only active transport requires energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the process of haemolysis?

options.text: Shrinking of red blood cells in hypertonic solution
Bursting of red blood cells in hypotonic solution
Normal functioning of red blood cells in isotonic solution
Swelling of red blood cells in isotonic solution

questions.explanation: Haemolysis refers to the bursting of red blood cells when they are placed in a hypotonic solution, causing water to enter the cells rapidly. This leads to cell lysis and the release of hemoglobin.

distractorRationale.a: This describes crenation, not haemolysis.
distractorRationale.c: This describes normal conditions for red blood cells.

options.text: It occurs until equilibrium is reached
It is a form of active transport

questions.explanation: Diffusion occurs until equilibrium is reached, meaning that molecules continue to move until their concentrations are equal on both sides of a membrane. It is a passive process that does not require energy.

distractorRationale.c: Diffusion occurs in liquids and solids as well, not just gases.

questions.explanation: Osmosis specifically requires a semi-permeable membrane to allow the movement of water while restricting solute movement. This is essential for maintaining proper cell function.

distractorRationale.b: Active transport does not require a semi-permeable membrane but rather specific transport proteins.
